content: 1. Fexinidazole inhibits the enzyme CYP3A4, which can increase the risk of adverse effects when co-administered with drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 2. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Idelalisib, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates or use alternative therapies. 4. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of drugs like infigratinib, irinotecan, and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Iron dextran complex and iron sucrose reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Isotretinoin and tetracycline are contraindicated due to an unknown mechanism that increases the risk of pseudotumor cerebri. 7. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Ivosidenib decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic efficacy. 10. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 11. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Magnesium chloride, magnesium citrate, magnesium hydroxide, magnesium oxide, and magnesium sulfate reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Mebendazole increases the toxicity of metronidazole, potentially leading to toxic epidermal necrolysis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Tetracycline and methoxyflurane should not be co-administered due to the risk of nephrotoxicity from pharmacodynamic synergism. 17. Tetracycline and methyl aminolevulinate increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, enhancing photosensitizing effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Tetracycline reduces the effects of microbiota oral by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral. 19. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of midazolam intranasal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of midazolam intranasal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Bismuth subsalicylate reduces minocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Tetracycline reduces the effects of nafcillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. 29. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. 30. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor for adverse effects. 31. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor for adverse effects. 32. Tetracycline reduces the effects of oxacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Bismuth subsalicylate reduces oxytetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Tetracycline and palovarotene should not be co-administered due to the risk of benign intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) associated with systemic retinoid use. 37. Tetracycline increases the effects of pancuronium by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. 39. Tetracycline reduces the effects of penicillin G aqueous by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. 41. Tetracycline reduces the effects of penicillin VK by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Phenobarbital decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Phenytoin decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Metronidazole increases pimozide levels by decreasing its metabolism, leading to a risk of QT interval prolongation. This combination is contraindicated. 45. Polysaccharide iron reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Primidone decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Metronidazole and propylene glycol should not be co-administered due to a disulfiram-like reaction caused by decreased metabolism. 48. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Tetracycline increases the effects of rapacuronium by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Tetracycline increases the effects of rocuronium by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Selinexor and metronidazole should not be co-administered due to the risk of neurological toxicities. Avoid combining selinexor with other medications that may cause dizziness or confusion. 53. Rose hips reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. 55. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. 56. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of siponimod with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor is not recommended. 58. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Sodium bicarbonate reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. 60. Sodium citrate/citric acid reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. 61. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium.
